family.note: Parents' instruction opens the wisdom collection; keep the image explaining its value.
The instruction to children includes the quoted commandment and its attached promise.
The household teaching also addresses fathers' responsibility not to provoke children.
Keep both instructions to spouses together; the husband's love and rejection of bitterness matter.
Keep Israel's confession and love of God with the teaching of children, so the words shared at home have their covenant context.
Care for widows is the setting; retain the opening call to honor widows with the family's responsibility.
Household provision appears in the discussion of support for widows; it is not a judgment on unavoidable poverty.
Ruth speaks to her mother-in-law Naomi after bereavement; this is family loyalty, not a wedding speech.
The psalm describes children as a gift; do not frame it as a guarantee of fertility or a measure of worth.
A concise proverb about affection and honor across generations.
The instruction explicitly includes care and respect for an aging mother.
Wisdom's picture of building a house invites reflection on cultivating a home, not a promise of wealth.

relationships.note: Jesus addresses his disciples; retain the link between mutual love and discipleship.
Paul describes love within teaching about the church's gifts; it applies beyond romantic relationships.
Forgiveness is grounded in God's forgiveness in Christ.
Keep compassion, bearing with one another, forgiveness and love together.
A connected sequence of sincere love, mutual honor, perseverance and practical hospitality.
Jesus' instruction sits within teaching on loving enemies, not merely returning favors.
Keep the example of Christ and care for a person in need with the call to love in action.
Love and prayer for enemies reflect the Father's generosity; this does not require remaining in danger.
Keep the call to walk worthily with humility, patience and unity in peace.
Retain both the listening instruction and the reason human anger is inadequate.
A practical contrast about responding gently in conflict, not a guarantee that conflict will stop.
Friendship and kinship are described in adversity as well as ordinary life.

work.note: Commit work to the Lord; read with the chapter's teaching that human plans remain subject to God.
Contrast effort with empty talk; a wisdom observation, not a guarantee of financial success.
The proverb values skillful work rather than promising every worker promotion.
Agricultural work contrasts with chasing empty pursuits.
Keep God's work and glory with the prayer to establish human work; this closing prayer sits within a psalm about life's limits.
Enjoyment of ordinary labor is described as God's gift within reflection on time.
Wholehearted action is set against the limits of mortal life; retain that reason.
Keep brotherly love with the connected appeal to a quiet life, honest work and conduct toward outsiders.
The instruction addresses disorderly busybodies in the community, not people unable to work.
Keep perseverance in doing good with the opportunity to serve others.
Honest labor is connected to sharing with those in need, not simply personal gain.
Keep gifts entrusted for others with the concrete examples of speech and service, God's supplied strength and the purpose of glorifying God.

money.note: Keep freedom from the love of money with God's presence and the response of trust.
Retain the contrast between godliness, possessions and basic necessities.
The warning concerns wanting riches and loving money, not money itself being evil.
Instructions to the wealthy include humility, uncertain riches and generosity together.
Wisdom praises generosity; do not present giving as an investment scheme.
Keep the paired contrasts: modest means with reverence and a simple meal with love.
A good name and the shared Creator of rich and poor belong together.
The generous person's sharing with the poor is the proverb's concrete action.
Kindness to the poor is valued before God; avoid implying a guaranteed cash return.
Paul discusses a collection for others; keep willing giving beside the sowing image.
Keep earthly and heavenly treasure together with the connection to the heart.
Jesus warns against covetousness before the parable of the rich fool.

decisions.note: Keep asking for wisdom with the connected instruction to ask in faith rather than double-mindedness.
The psalmist describes God's word guiding a path, not supplying a prediction of the future.
Keep trust, humility about understanding and acknowledging God together.
Guarding the heart belongs to counsel about speech, sight and conduct.
The prophet's answer concerns justice, kindness and walking humbly rather than transactional offerings.
Keep offering one's life beside renewed thinking and discerning God's will.
Careful living and use of time lead into understanding the Lord's will.
The proverb holds human planning beside God's direction.
Retain wisdom's qualities and its fruit in peacemaking.
Wise conduct and gracious speech toward outsiders belong together.
The prayer asks for wisdom through awareness of life's limits.
Seeking counsel is a practical part of making plans.

rest.note: Jesus comforts disciples before his departure; peace is not the absence of every difficulty.
Keep prayer and thanksgiving beside the peace that guards hearts and thoughts.
Retain the call to trust alongside the promise in this communal song.
Jesus' invitation includes learning from him and his yoke; preserve the complete invitation.
The psalmist's closing prayer expresses confidence while lying down.
Keep humility before God with casting anxiety on him.
A closing prayer for peace at all times and in all ways.
The opening shepherd imagery includes provision, rest and guidance.
The proverb gives a concrete role to a good word in anxiety.
Keep the kingdom priority with counsel about tomorrow; this is not a promise of an easy life.
Keep fear and trust with the psalmist's praise of God's word.
The psalmist addresses his soul while waiting on God.

hardship.note: God's nearness to the brokenhearted belongs with the cry for help.
Hope is voiced within lament over devastation; it does not erase the lament.
The psalmist speaks to his downcast soul in an unresolved lament.
Keep the sequence from suffering through perseverance to hope and God's love.
Paul describes hardship with an eternal perspective rather than denying present suffering.
Keep blessing persecutors with rejoicing and weeping alongside others; practical accompaniment belongs beside assurance in hardship.
Preserve the whole lament from repeated questions through petition to trust and praise; grief is voiced rather than bypassed.
The opening confession of refuge introduces a psalm describing upheaval.
Keep the psalmist's desire for God beside the failure of flesh and heart.
Keep the reason for endurance and its maturing purpose; do not demand cheerful feelings in grief.
The assurance concerns God's love in Christ, not freedom from loss or suffering.
The vision of God's dwelling provides the setting for the future end of tears and death.

gratitude.note: Keep rejoicing, prayer and thanksgiving together; giving thanks in circumstances does not call evil good.
The opening summons gives enduring loving kindness as its reason.
Words and deeds are connected to thanksgiving through Jesus.
Rejoicing belongs within a thanksgiving song for the Lord's saving work.
Praise belongs with doing good and sharing; retain both verses.
Retain the opening warning against deception with the source of good gifts.
Keep praise and remembering with the complete list of benefits that follows.
Keep the connected instructions through thanksgiving and mutual submission.
Walking in Christ and being rooted in faith culminate in thanksgiving.
The invitation to give thanks includes God's goodness and enduring faithfulness.
A communal invitation to joyful worship and thanksgiving.
Keep rejoicing with gentleness toward everyone and the Lord's nearness; the adjacent prayer passage has its own place in Worry and rest.

faith.note: Keep Jesus' sympathetic priesthood with the invitation to approach for mercy and help.
Nearness to those who call in truth is paired with reverence and the cry for help.
Keep salvation by grace through faith, the exclusion of boasting and the resulting good works together; works are the response, not the source of salvation.
Keep the contrast with public performance beside the instruction to pray privately.
Both suffering and cheerfulness are occasions for turning toward God.
Watchfulness and thanksgiving lead into prayer for the opportunity to speak of Christ.
Prayer's confidence is explicitly according to God's will, not a blank promise of any outcome.
A morning prayer offers a daily rhythm of speaking and watching expectantly.
Keep the Spirit's help in weakness with God's knowledge of the Spirit's intercession.
The closing prayer asks to be searched and led, rather than merely reassured.
Abiding in Christ provides the setting for the vine and branches picture.
Keep walking by faith inside Paul's connected statement about confidence, bodily life and being with the Lord; verse 8 completes the statement around verse 7.
